invalid_if: A charge is added after the consumer has placed the order
The total price is not broken down before purchase
name: Shipping Charges
title: Shipping Charges
text:
Shipping charges are applied as follows.
(a) The shipping charge payable on an order is shown to the consumer before the order is placed, and no charge is added afterwards.
(b) Where a shipping charge is waived above an order value, that value is stated on the platform.
(c) Applicable taxes on the shipping charge are shown separately, and the invoice issued to the consumer complies with Section 31 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
(d) Where cash on delivery is offered, any additional charge for it is shown before the order is placed.
(e) Where an order is cancelled or returned in the circumstances set out in the Refund and Cancellation Policy, the treatment of the shipping charge is as stated in that Policy.

legal_basis.note: The total price of goods or services must be broken down, showing all compulsory and voluntary charges such as delivery, postage, handling and conveyance

legal_basis.act: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017

legal_basis.note: Unfair trade practice, including a charge not disclosed before purchase

source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; CGST Act, 2017; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
authoring_note: Limb (a) reflects the price-breakdown duty in the E-Commerce Rules. Undisclosed charges added at checkout are the single most frequently complained-of practice under these Rules.
